Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. The fielding team has taken their positions as well. Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana walk out to open the batting innings. Mahika Gaur has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

The Indians had a dream start to their innings as Renuka Singh dismissed two of their batters in the first over. After that, some poor bowling and fielding helped the opposition batters to put up a strong partnership. A couple of dropped catches and misfields also didn’t work in their favor. It was the debutant Saika who got the main wicket of Danni Wyatt. Shreyanka Patil put an end to Heather’s innings and claimed her first wicket. Renuka Singh dismissed Natalie Sciver-Brunt to clinch her third of the day. However, the target for them is 198. Join us in a bit as India Women prepare themselves for a mammoth chase.  Will they be able to pull off a miracle chase or will the visitors dominate? We will find out soon.

England Women had been dealt a couple of fatal blows in the first over itself as Sophia Dunkley and Alice Capsey were dismissed in consecutive balls. After that, it was all about the sensible yet aggressive batting from the two amazing players, Danni Wyatt and Natalie Sciver-Brunt. They made sure that their team was back in the game and took the attack to the Indian bowlers. They were pouncing at any chance they got and were rewarded well with boundaries. Natalie Sciver-Brunt continued her onslaught along with Heather Knight until the latter had to depart. Amy Jones also had no plans to play safe and started throwing her hands from the get-go giving her team an explosive end.

What a comeback it is for England Women as they end their innings powering themselves to 197 on the board courtesy of the strong batting partnership between Danni Wyatt and Natalie Sciver-Brunt with an explosive end by Amy Jones.

OUT! The England inning comes to an end with a wicket off the final delivery. Full toss in middle, Amy Jones looks to clear the fence but launches one straight towards Jemimah Rodrigues at deep mid-wicket. Jemimah Rodrigues misjudged the flight of it initially as she runs it but adjusts well int he end to hop backwards and take this one not that far away from the fence. England Women have scored 197 in their quota of 20 overs.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin as the two umpires make their way out to the middle. The fielding team makes their way out to the middle after some last-minute instructions from their skipper. Both teams and the match officials match out for the national anthems. It will be the national anthem of England followed by the Indian national anthem.

India Women (Playing XI) - Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Jemimah Rodrigues, Harmanpreet Kaur (C), Deepti Sharma, Richa Ghosh (WK), Shreyanka Patil, Kanika Ahuja, Pooja Vastrakar, Renuka Singh, Saika Ishaque.
England Women (Playing XI) - Danni Wyatt, Sophia Dunkley, Alice Capsey, Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Heather Knight (C), Amy Jones (WK), Freya Kemp, Sophie Ecclestone, Sarah Glenn, Lauren Bell, Mahika Gaur.
Heather Knight says that they will have to go out and bat well and talks about the excess bounce on this pitch. She adds that the team will look to go out there and score some runs doing so.

Harmanpreet Kaur says that they will bowl as they want to chase down the target and put pressure on the opposition while being confident about her batting. She mentions Shreyanka Patil and Saika Ishaque are the debutants for today. She adds that she wants to get ahead with a win.
TOSS - The captains are out in the middle. The coin is flipped into the air and lands in favor of India Women. They have elected to BOWL first.

India Women on the other hand have the home advantage and have built a very strong-looking squad with the likes of Harmanpreet Kaur, Smriti Mandhana, Shafali Verma, Richa Ghosh, Jemimah Rodrigues, and Deepti Sharma ready to score some runs. The bowling unit is equally strong carried by Pooja Vastrakar, Saika Ishaque, Renuka Singh, and Titas Sadhu. The only reason to worry is that this team is playing their first international game after three months. Will the squad led by Harmanpreet Kaur be able to find their rhythm soon and take the lead in the series? We will find out soon. Toss and team news to follow.

Have to say the hosts could be the favourites heading into this encounter but England has a strong side and they are well and truly capable of beating anyone on their day. Led by the experienced, Heather Knight she has to choose the squad from an arsenal of young and experienced players. Natalie Sciver-Brunt, Danni Wyatt, Maia Bouchier, Alice Capsey, and Bess Heath will look forward to showcasing their talent from the start of the series. Their bowling unit is equally strong with the likes of Sophie Ecclestone, Lauren Bell, Mahika Gaur, Freya Kemp, and Sarah Glenn among others. We will have to wait and see what combination Heather Knight opts for but one thing is for certain this squad looks strong and very well capable of beating any team.

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. The Indian Women's cricket team is back in action and they are up against England. They'll be playing three T20Is followed by one Test. The first T20I will be played at Mumbai and both sides will be eager to get off with a win in this contest which is expected to be full of excitement.

In the aftermath of clinching the Gold medal at the Asian Games 2023, India Women eagerly return to action, hosting England Women in a high-stakes cricket showdown. Following their triumph over Bangladesh Women in the last series, the hosts have made some changes, especially on the bowling front. The dynamic opening partnership of Shafali Verma and Smriti Mandhana promises to be a pivotal force, while Jemimah Rodrigues and captain Harmanpreet Kaur fortify the middle order. The lineup gains additional firepower from Richa Ghosh and Pooja Vastrakar, who can launch the ball a long way. Pooja, doubling as a pace bowler alongside Renuka Singh and rising star Titas Sadhu, adds strength to India's bowling arsenal. Deepti Sharma, with her spin prowess, aims to trouble batters while contributing crucial runs with the bat. Young talents like Shreyanka Patil and Mannat Kashyap, showcasing skills in India Women-A's encounter against England Women-A, might get an opportunity to shine on the grand stage. On the flip side, England Women, eager to rebound after a T20I series loss to Sri Lanka Women, bring a formidable squad. Danni Wyatt, a reliable opener, and in-form Maia Bouchier set the tone at the top. Alice Capsey, Heather Knight, and Amy Jones aspire to navigate Indian conditions and anchor the middle order. Mahika Gaur and Natalie Sciver-Brunt lead the pace attack, complemented by the spin expertise of Sophie Ecclestone, ​​​​supported by Charlie Dean. With both teams boasting quality all-rounders, the series promises intense competition. England Women, recalling their whitewash of India Women in the last tour, seeks inspiration, while the Women in Blue, now a formidable force, aim to avenge that defeat. The series opener is poised to reveal which team seizes the early advantage in this anticipated battle of cricketing prowess.
